extracted.intended_audience: journalists and press professionals (and readers interested in press ethics)
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and summarize the proposed international code of ethics for newspapermen as reported by the U.N. sub-commission: principles, prohibitions, and procedural/organizational stances governing journalistic conduct, freedom, and professional responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful and conscientious work
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft code "calls for truthful conscientious work" by newsmen in their reporting and commentary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting must seek and present the truth; journalists should be diligent and conscientious in gathering and presenting information. The code frames truthfulness and conscientiousness as foundational professional obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of slander, libel and plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: The code "declamss that slander, libel and plagiarism are serious professional offenses."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willful calumny, unfounded accusations, and plagiarism are explicitly identified as serious professional misconduct. Journalists should avoid defamatory statements and must credit sources appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking and non-distortion of essential facts
rubrics_metrics.description: "They should check all [facts] to the best of their ability, no fact should... no essential fact should be deliberately distorted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are required to verify information before publication, use due diligence in confirmation, and must not intentionally distort or omit essential facts. Submission of reviews or corroborating material (as in congressional hearings cited) is an example of supporting accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for the reputation and privacy of individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reputation of individuals should be respected and distinguished from public curiosity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should balance public interest against undue invasion of personal reputation or privacy. Sensationalism that serves mere curiosity should be avoided; treatment of individuals must be fair and respectful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of reply / opportunity for response
rubrics_metrics.description: "An opportunity should be given for reply."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When individuals or organizations are criticized or accused, the code requires giving them reasonable opportunity to comment or respond within the outlet’s coverage; this supports fairness and correction of errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional secrecy and protection of confidential sources
rubrics_metrics.description: "Professional secrecy should be observed in matter revealed in confidence and this..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information disclosed to journalists in confidence should be protected; journalists should guard sources when confidentiality was promised and reveal only when ethically justified (e.g., overriding public interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of responsibility / accountability for published material
rubrics_metrics.description: "Those who make public an information or comment should assume full responsibility" (responsibility rests with those publishing, not with government).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors, editors, and publishers must accept responsibility for the accuracy and consequences of material they put in the public domain; disclaimers do not absolve professional responsibility. The code emphasizes professional accountability rather than governmental enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary nature and self-regulation of the code
rubrics_metrics.description: The draft states that "no government should attempt to enforce the code" and treats the text as "a guide for the conduct of those who wanted to follow it," not a binding instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code is intended as a profession-led, voluntary ethical guide. It recommends that journalists and press organizations adopt and refine standards themselves (including via proposed international conferences) rather than submit to government-imposed controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense of press freedom and opposition to intimidation or imprisonment of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporting denounces imprisonment and intimidation of reporters (citing William Oatis' imprisonment as "intimidation at its worst") and asserts the need to safeguard the truth in reporting and gathering information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic ethics are linked to preserving freedom of information: the code calls for protection of journalists from state repression and for resisting measures that limit the independent gathering and dissemination of news. The profession should oppose legal or extralegal actions that intimidate or imprison reporters doing their work.
